RagShortTexts: The Teutonic Order forged a monastic state in Prussia and Livonia under the black cross banner.

Variants.Content: The Teutonic Knights (Deutscher Orden) spearheaded the Northern Crusades across the Baltic wilderness. Clad in white mantles with plain black crosses, they erected red-brick convents (Ordensburgen) across Prussia and Livonia, converting pagans by iron discipline and founding an autonomous monastic state.

Backed by imperial Golden Bulls, the Grand Master directed secular crusaders from the Rhine and Westphalia. Monopolizing Baltic amber and sea lanes, the Order established efficient bureaucratic administration.
Through dense pine swamps, Teutonic lances ride down pagan resistance. Communities that reject baptism see their sacred groves felled and replaced by stone bastions demanding tithes.
